matthew.17.p1.b1.text: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John the brother of James, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.

matthew.17.p1.b2.text: There He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as the light.

matthew.17.p2.b1.text: Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus.

matthew.17.p2.b2.text: Lord, it is good for us to be here.

matthew.17.p2.b3.text: If You wish, I will put up three shelters —one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.

matthew.17.p3.b1.text: While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud enveloped them,

matthew.17.p3.b2.text: This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!

matthew.17.p3.b3.text: When the disciples heard this, they fell facedown in terror.

matthew.17.p4.b1.text: Get up, … Do not be afraid.

matthew.17.p4.b2.text: And when they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.

matthew.17.p5.b1.text: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them,

matthew.17.p5.b2.text: Do not tell anyone about this vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.

matthew.17.p5.b3.text: Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?

matthew.17.p6.b1.text: Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things.

matthew.17.p6.b2.text: But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but have done to him whatever they wished.

matthew.17.p6.b3.text: In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer at their hands.

matthew.17.p6.b4.text: Then the disciples understood that He was speaking to them about John the Baptist.

matthew.17.p7.b1.text: When they came to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus and knelt before Him.

matthew.17.p7.b2.text: Lord, have mercy on my son, … He has seizures and is suffering terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.

matthew.17.p7.b3.text: I brought him to Your disciples, but they could not heal him.”

matthew.17.p8.b1.text: O unbelieving and perverse generation! … How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you?

matthew.17.p8.b2.text: Bring the boy here to Me.

matthew.17.p8.b3.text: Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy,

matthew.17.p8.b4.text: and he was healed from that moment.

matthew.17.p9.b1.text: Afterward the disciples came to Jesus privately and asked,

matthew.17.p9.b2.text: Why couldn’t we drive it out?

matthew.17.p9.b3.text: Because you have so little faith, … if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move.

matthew.17.p9.b4.text: Nothing will be impossible for you.

matthew.17.p10.b1.text: When they gathered together in Galilee, Jesus told them,

matthew.17.p10.b2.text: The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men. They will kill Him, and on the third day He will be raised to life.

matthew.17.p10.b3.text: And the disciples were deeply grieved.

matthew.17.p11.b1.text: After they had arrived in Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and asked,

matthew.17.p11.b2.text: Does your Teacher pay the two drachmas?

matthew.17.p11.b4.text: What do you think, Simon? … From whom do the kings of the earth collect customs and taxes: from their own sons, or from others?

matthew.17.p12.b3.text: But so that we may not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a four-drachma coin.

matthew.17.p12.b4.text: Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.
